item.title: You Can Unlock Lots Of Free Stuff In Pokemon Go’s Halloween 2026 Event
item.description:
Halloween may be over, but Pokemon Go is still celebrating the spooky holiday with its annual Halloween event. This year's festivities take place across two parts that run into early November, each of which will offer new Pokemon, Research tasks, and other bonuses.

To help you prepare, here's everything you need to know about Pokemon Go's Halloween 2026 event.

In This Article
  • Halloween Part I
    • Event Schedule
    • Featured Pokemon
    • Timed And Field Research
    • Chandelure Super Mega Raid Day
    • Bonuses
  • Halloween Part II
    • Event Schedule
    • Featured Pokemon
    • Timed And Field Research

Halloween Part I

Event Schedule

The first part of this year's Halloween event kicks off at 10 AM local time on October 27 and runs until 10 AM local time on November 1.

Featured Pokemon

Like previous years, a handful of new costumed Pokemon will make their debut during the Halloween festivities. Part I will introduce three costume-wearing monsters to catch:

  • Pikachu wearing a hat and capelet
  • Zubat wearing a top hat
  • Sinistea wearing a bow

You can encounter the aforementioned Pokemon in the wild or as one-star Raid bosses. Shiny variants will also be appearing throughout the event.

In addition, some costume-wearing Pokemon from previous years will appear in the wild once again, as will other creepy monsters like Duskull and Misdreavus.

Wild Encounters

  • Zubat wearing a top hat
  • Misdreavus
  • Duskull
  • Piplup wearing a Halloween Mischief costume
  • Drifblim wearing a Halloween Mischief costume
  • Pumpkaboo

Raid Bosses

One-Star

  • Pikachu wearing a hat and capelet
  • Sinistea wearing a bow

Timed And Field Research

Pokemon Go is offering a free Timed Research for all players. Log in before Part I ends on November 1 to claim the Research, which will be completed automatically and net you the following rewards:

  • Rare Candies (6)
  • An encounter with Pikachu wearing a hat and capelet

Some Halloween-themed Field Research tasks will also be available during the event. You can claim these by spinning PokeStops, and they'll offer various rewards when completed, including additional encounters with the featured Pokemon.

Chandelure Super Mega Raid Day

A spooky new Mega-Evolved Pokemon is making its debut on Halloween: Mega Chandelure.

The ghost/fire type will appear as a Super Mega Raid boss on October 31 from 2-5 PM local time, marking your first chance to get this Mega-Evolved form in Pokemon Go. Not only that, but you'll have increased odds of encountering shiny Chandelure from these Raids, and any Chandelure that you catch will have Mega Level 1 already unlocked.

A few other bonuses will be available during this mini-event. The number of Remote Raids you can join is being increased to 20 for a limited time, and you'll be able to get up to six free Raid Passes when you spin the Photo Disc at Gyms.

Bonuses

  • Remote Raid limit increased to 20 (October 30-31)
  • Receive up to six free Raid Passes from spinning Gym Photo Discs
  • Chandelure caught from Super Mega Raids will have Mega Level 1 unlocked
  • Increased chance of encountering shiny Chandelure from Super Mega Raids

Bonuses

Like past years, Pokemon Go will receive a spooky makeover during the Halloween event. The usual nighttime background music will be replaced by a remix of the infamous Lavender Town theme, and Gyms and PokeStops will be decked out in Halloween decorations.

On top of that, the game will offer its own version of trick-or-treating. As you play, you'll periodically notice gift boxes on the map. Tap on these and you'll receive candy or initiate an encounter with a costumed Pokemon.

Finally, a few additional bonuses will unlock as you level up the event's Go Pass. Hit rank 10 and you'll receive extra candy for catching Pokemon, and you'll earn bonus Stardust on top of that if you reach rank 20.

Go Pass Tier 1 (Rank 10)

  • 2x candy for catching Pokemon
  • Go Pass Deluxe: 3x candy for catching Pokemon

Go Pass Tier 2 (Rank 20)

  • 2x Stardust for catching Pokemon
  • Go Pass Deluxe: 3x Stardust for catching Pokemon

Halloween Part II

Event Schedule

This year's Halloween festivities will continue into early November. Part II begins at 10 AM local time on November 1 and runs until 8 PM local time on November 5.

Featured Pokemon

Like Part I, a new Pokemon is debuting during the second leg of this year's Halloween event: shiny Greavard. This marks the first time you'll have a chance to encounter this shiny variant in Pokemon Go.

Mega Sableye is also getting a power boost. Beginning with Part II, you'll be able to power up the Pokemon's Mega Level up to Super Max Level, which means it'll have access to an additional Charged Attack–Night Shade+--while it's Mega Evolved.

A few other themed Pokemon will also be available during the event. Costumed versions of Gengar and Rowlet will appear in the wild, as will ghost types like Litwick.

Wild Encounters

  • Gengar wearing a Spooky Festival costume
  • Litwick
  • Rowlet wearing a Pokemon Halloween costume
  • Greavard

Raid Bosses

One-Star

  • Pikachu wearing a hat and capelet
  • Sinistea wearing a bow

Timed And Field Research

Another free Timed Research will be available during the second part of this year's Halloween event. Log in before November 5 to claim the Timed Research, which will be completed automatically and offer the following rewards:

  • Rare Candies (6)
  • An encounter with Sinistea wearing a bow

A variety of Field Research tasks will also be available. These can be claimed from PokeStops and will reward you with encounters with the event's featured Pokemon upon completion.

October may be coming to an end soon, but Pokemon Go has plenty of activities lined up for next month, including a global Wild Area event and a Pawniard Community Day. Check back soon for our November events roundup.

item.title: Everything New In Fortnite Treasure Hunters Mini-Season
item.description:
One Piece is taking over Fortnite for the next five weeks as part of the game's now-annual November mini-season, which swaps out the current Battle Royale island for a smaller new pirate-themed one. Dubbed Fortnite Treasure Hunters, the new season is now live and will also focus heavily on music collabs with A$AP Rocky, Lil Uzi Vert, Hatsune Miku and Kasane Teto--Epic isn't putting all its eggs in one cartoon basket like it did last year with its Simpsons season.

Epic started doing these mini-seasons back in Chapter 4 with the original Fortnite OG event, and that one went so well that the company decided to make it a tradition. With Fortnite facing down the launch of GTA VI in late November, it needed some serious firepower--and One Piece, which has been one of the most requested Fortnite collabs ever, certainly qualifies.

Let's take a look at the details.

Fortnite Treasure Hunters battle pass

The Treasure Hunters battle pass is not a full collab pass, unlike the Simpsons and Star Wars ones from 2025. Instead, the pass includes three anime-themed Fortnite people, and two One Piece characters--Nico Robin and Portgas D. Ace--and one regular new Fortnite guy The rest of the rather robust roster of One Piece skins will be in the shop, which we'll talk about later.

The Fortnite original characters in the pass include anime makeovers of Jonesy and Syd, as well as a rare re-do of Charlotte from the Chapter 2 Season 8 battle pass. The final skin is Captain X, who will be unlockable on November 21 via weekly quests.

Welcome to Skull Island (sort of)

The current BR island is being replaced with Crossbones Isle, a smaller island that has a max capacity of 80 players, down from the usual 100--same as the Springfield map last year. The new map has a lot more water than the Chapter 7 map did, and it's filled with new locations based on One Piece, like Arlong Park and Windmill Village, as well as spots based on the music collabs. There's a new POI with a battleship in it, for example, which belongs to A$AP Rocky. Lil Uzi Vert, Kasane Teto, and Hatsune Miku should also get their own POIs as the season goes on.

Item shop collabs

Aside from Robin and Ace, all other collabs are in the item shop. The One Piece cosmetics will drop piece by piece during the season, with Luffy, Nami, and Usopp available when Treasure Hunters season starts. Zoro, Sanji, and Chopper (as a sidekick) will drop on November 7, and Buggy the Star Clown lands in the shop on November 13.

For the music collabs, A$AP Rocky hits the chop on November 5, followed by Lil Uzi Vert on November 12, and Kasane Teto and a new pirate-themed Hatsune Miku on November 14. It could be that one of these artists will be headlining the next music pass, which is slated to start November 12, but we don't know yet.

The new music pass was supposed to begin on November 1, but Epic abruptly delayed it by three months just a few days before it was supposed to start. But after a rather intense backlash by Fortnite Crew subscribers, who have already been receiving significantly less value for their money this year, Epic changed its tune and announced a new music pass would start on November 12.

Find free Fortnite skins by opening chests

It may be that Epic tried to cancel the music pass because they're giving away a lot of stuff for free during Treasure Hunters season. Opening chests in Battle Royale has a chance to grant various free items, including cosmetics like an A$AP Rocky skin, a Mercedes SUV, and a jam track.

But the best item is the Pirate Shop token, which grants you the entire item shop for free for two weeks after its activated. Yes, that's right, if you find this one you can claim everything in the item shop without paying anything for 14 days. With GTA on the horizon, Epic has switched into Willy Wonka mode to keep folks engaged

New weapons, loot, and sprites

In addition to the POIs, each of these collaborations will have new weapons, sprites and other loot you can find.

  • Gum-Gum Fruit: Grants Luffy's stretching powers
  • Flame-Flame Fruit: Grants Ace's fire-based abilities
  • Zoro's Three Sword Style: Allows you to battle foes with three katanas
  • Usopp's Slingshot: Essentially a scopeless sniper
  • A$AP Rocky's Shock Rocket: It's like the old Shockwave Rocket Launcher but it fires additional rockets at the ground as you launch away
  • Gilded Dragoon Shotgun: A heavy shotgun that only holds one shot before requiring a reload
  • Bundlebuss Repeater Rifle: Mid-range assault rifle
  • Nami's Tangerine and Meat on a Stick: New healing items

Chapter 7 finale event

Chapter 7 will end with some kind of major live event on December 5. We don't know anything yet about what'll be included, but these things are always pretty wild.
